ch8.intro: The comparison is a dot product: multiply the two vectors component by component, then add up the products. Two vectors that point the same way give a high score; vectors pointing in opposite directions give a low one, even a negative one.
ch8.formulaNote: score = q1 x k1 + q2 x k2 + ... + q8 x k8, one component of the query times the matching component of the key.
ch8.scores: With “{word}”, the query of “il” and the key of “animal” give a score of {a}<c1></c1>, against {b} with the key of “boulevard”<c2></c2>. Each dot of the plate is the product of one component of the query and the matching component of the key; the score is their sum.
ch8.rounding: The products on the plate are rounded to two decimal places.
ch8.labelAnimal: The 8 products of “il” and “animal”, sentence ending in “{word}”: {list}
ch8.labelBoulevard: The 8 products of “il” and “boulevard”, sentence ending in “{word}”: {list}
ch8.caption: The eight products, component by component, then their sum. <c1></c1> Score of “il” with “animal”. <c2></c2> Score of “il” with “boulevard”. Sentence ending in “{word}”.
ch8.formula: score = q1 x k1 + q2 x k2 + ... + q8 x k8
ch8.reading: Filled dot: positive product. Empty ring: negative product. The area is proportional to the absolute value.
ch8.next: These raw scores can take any value: they have to be turned into weights.

ch9.statement: With “{word}”, “il” gives <n>{share}</n> of its attention to “{first}”.
ch9.intro: Raw scores can take any value. Softmax turns them into weights between 0 and 1 that add up to exactly 1: a recipe.
ch9.scores: With “{word}”, the scores {firstScore}<c1></c1> for “{first}” and {secondScore}<c2></c2> for “{second}” become {firstShare} and {secondShare}. The other {others} words share the remaining {rest}.
ch9.sum: The thirteen weights always add up to exactly 1, or {total}.
ch9.waffleLabel: {dots} dots: {first} for “{firstWord}”, {second} for “{secondWord}”, {rest} for the other {others} words.

table.title: Word, raw score, weight, sentence ending in “{word}”

ch9.caption: The recipe: 100 dots, one per percent. <c1></c1> The weight of the word that receives the most attention. <c2></c2> The weight of the second. The other {others} words share the rest.
ch9.reading: One dot per percent: the orange dots belong to the word that receives the most attention.
ch9.next: All that remains is to blend the values according to these weights.

ch10.intro: Each value is multiplied by its weight, then everything is added up. The blend is then added to the vector of “il”.
ch10.valueNote: A value is not a key: the key decides whether a word gets chosen, the value is what it passes on once chosen.
ch10.mix: The thirteen values are scaled by the weights of <link>chapter 9</link>. With “{word}”, the blend<c1></c1> is made of {firstShare} of “{first}”<c2></c2>, {secondShare} of “{second}” and {rest} of the other words.
ch10.addNote: The blend is added to the vector of “il”: it does not replace it.
ch10.figureLabel: The 13 values, weighted by attention, merge into one for “il”: “{first}” {firstShare}, “{second}” {secondShare}, the rest {rest}.

conclusion.tired: After attention, “il” carries the information of “animal” and “tired”: it now stands for the tired animal.
conclusion.wide: After attention, “il” carries the information of “boulevard” and “wide”: it now stands for the boulevard that is too wide.
